Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verse 2–4:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who are wrapped up, arise and warn﴾. That is, warn the disbelievers of Makkah.

﴿And your Lord, glorify﴾. Magnify Him above what the idol-worshippers say.

﴿And your garments, purify﴾. Qatadah and Mujahid said: "Purify your self." [from sin] [[In "B": "from sins".]] So he referred to the self by means of the garment. This is also the view of Ibrahim, al-Dahhak, al-Sha'bi and al-Zuhri. ʿIkrimah said: Ibn ʿAbbas was asked about his saying: "And your garments, purify," and he said: "Do not wear them over disobedience or over treachery." Then he said: "Have you not heard the saying of Ghaylan ibn Salamah al-Thaqafi:

*And, by the praise of God, I have not worn the garment of a wicked man,*
*nor do I veil myself with treachery.*" [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 29/145. al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/326) added its attribution to Sa'id ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Anbari in al-Waqf wa'l-Ibtida', and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

The Arabs say, in describing a man as truthful and faithful: "He has clean garments," and they say of one who betrays: "He has soiled garments." Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: "Do not wear them over treachery, nor over injustice, nor over sin; wear them while you are righteous [generous] [[Addition from "A".]] and pure."

Abu Rawq narrated from al-Dahhak its meaning: "And your deeds, set right."

al-Suddi said: It is said of a man when he is righteous: "Indeed, he has clean garments," and when he is wicked: "Indeed, he has filthy garments."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "And your heart and your intention, purify." al-Hasan and al-Qurazi said: "And your character, beautify."

Ibn Sirin and Ibn Zayd said: He commanded the purification of garments from the impurities with which prayer is not valid, because the polytheists [were] [[Addition from "B".]] neither purifying themselves nor purifying their garments. [[Ibn Jarir said (29/147) after mentioning this view and others: "This view stated by Ibn Sirin and Ibn Zayd is the most apparent of its meanings."]]

Tawus said: "And your garments, shorten," because shortening garments is a means of purifying them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verses 5–6:

﴿And the abomination, forsake it.﴾ Abu Ja'far, Hafs (on the authority of ʿAsim) and Yaʿqub read "wa-r-rujza" with a dammah on the rāʾ, while the others read it with a kasrah. The two are dialectal variants (lughatan) and their meaning is one. Mujahid, ʿIkrimah, Qatadah, al-Zuhri, Ibn Zayd and Abu Salamah said: by ar-rijz (abomination) is meant the idols. He said: forsake them and do not draw near to them.

It was also said: the zayn in it is a substitution for a sīn, and the Arabs interchange sīn and zayn because their points of articulation are close. The evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿So avoid the abomination of the idols﴾ [al-Hajj: 30].

It was narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that its meaning is: abandon the sins.

Abu al-ʿAliyah and al-Rabiʿ said: ar-rujz with a dammah on the rāʾ means the idol, and with a kasrah means the impurity and the disobedience.

al-Dahhak said: it means polytheism. al-Kalbi said: it means the punishment.

The figurative sense of the verse: forsake whatever deeds bring punishment upon you.

﴿And do not bestow favour in order to receive more﴾: that is, do not give your wealth seeking to be given more in return. This is the view of most of the exegetes. al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: this was specific to the Prophet ﷺ. al-Dahhak said: there are two kinds of gifts (ribaan), a lawful and an unlawful: the lawful is gifts, and the unlawful is usury (riba). Qatadah said: do not give anything out of desire for worldly recompense; rather give for your Lord and intend by it God. al-Hasan said: its meaning is: do not confer favour upon God by your deed, so that you consider it abundant. al-Rabiʿ said: do not regard your deed as great in your eyes, for whatever God has bestowed upon you and given you is little. Khusayf narrated from Mujahid: "and do not weaken to seek abundance of good," from the saying "a firm rope" (habl matin) when it is weak. Its evidence is the reading of Ibn Masʿud: "wa-la tamnun an tastakthira." Ibn Zayd said: its meaning is: do not bestow favour upon the people with prophethood, so that you take a reward for it or some worldly gain. [[al-Tabari narrated most of these sayings (29/148–150), then said, preferring: "The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying of whoever said: its meaning is: do not confer favour upon your Lord by considering your righteous deed as great. I say this is more correct because it comes in a context of verses in which God's command to His Prophet ﷺ to strive earnestly in calling to Him and to be patient over the harm he suffers in it was mentioned; so this is more fitting to be one of those types than to be of something else."]]

﴿And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels﴾, not human men. Who, then, could overpower the angels? ﴿And We have not made their number﴾, that is, their count in terms of fewness, ﴿except as a trial for those who disbelieve﴾, that is, as misguidance for them, so that they said what they said. ﴿That those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾, because it is written in the Torah and the Gospel that they are nineteen. ﴿And those who believe may increase in faith﴾, meaning those among the People of the Book who believe increase in their affirmation of Muhammad ﷺ when they find that what he said agrees with what is in their books. ﴿And those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt﴾, that is, will not be uncertain ﴿about their number﴾. ﴿And that those in whose hearts is disease﴾, meaning doubt and hypocrisy, ﴿and the disbelievers﴾ [the polytheists of Makkah] [[Omitted from "B".]] ﴿say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾, that is, what did He intend by this statement? And by "example" he means the statement itself.

﴿Thus﴾, that is, just as Allah misguides whoever denies the number of the guardians and guides whoever affirms it, ﴿Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾. Muqatil said: this is the response to Abu Jahl when he said: "Does Muhammad have only nineteen helpers?" Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verses 35–39:

﴿Indeed, it is one of the greatest (calamities)﴾. He means that Saqar is one of the great matters. The singular of al-Kubar is Kubra. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: by al-Kubar he meant the levels (darakat) of Jahannam, and they are seven: Jahannam, Laza, al-Hutama, al-Sa'ir, Saqar, al-Jahim, and al-Hawiyah.

﴿A warning to mankind﴾. He means the Fire is a warning to mankind. Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, Allah has not given a warning with anything more dreadful than it." It is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (nasb 'ala al-qat') from His saying "one of the greatest," because the latter is definite (ma'rifah) and "nadhiran" is indefinite (nakirah). Al-Khalil said: al-Nadhir is a verbal noun (masdar), like al-Nakir, and for this reason it is applied as an attribute to the feminine. It was also said: it is an attribute of Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, and its meaning is: "And We did not make the companions of the Fire except angels, a warning to mankind," that is, a warning to them. Abu Ruzayn said: it means "I am a warning to you from it, so beware of it." It was also said: it is an attribute of Muhammad ﷺ, and its meaning is: "O you who are wrapped up, arise and warn (nadhiran) mankind," [so warn] (this addition is from manuscript "a"), and this is the meaning of the saying of Ibn Zayd.

﴿For whoever among you wills﴾ is a substitute (badal) for His saying "for mankind," ﴿to advance﴾ toward good and obedience, ﴿or to lag behind﴾ from it toward evil and disobedience. The meaning is that the warning has reached each one of those who believed or disbelieved.

﴿Every soul, for what it has earned, is held in pledge﴾: held as a pledge in the Fire by its earnings, seized for its deeds.

﴿Except the companions of the right﴾: they are not held as pledges in the Fire for their sins, rather Allah forgives them. Qatadah said: all people are held in pledge except the companions of the right. And they differed concerning them: it is narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that they are the children of the Muslims.

Abu Zabyan narrated from Ibn Abbas: they are the angels.

Muqatil said: they are the people of Paradise who were on the right of Adam on the Day of the Covenant, when Allah said to them: "These are in Paradise, and I do not mind." And also from him: they are those who were given their books in their right hands. And also from him: they are those who were blessed (mayamin) regarding their own selves.

Al-Hasan said: they are the sincere Muslims. Al-Qasim (in manuscript "a": Abu al-Qasim) said: every soul is seized for its earnings, of good or evil, except one who relies on grace (al-fadl); and whoever relies on earning is held in pledge by it, and whoever relies on grace is not seized by it.

﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder﴾ — the admonitions of the Qur'an — ﴿turning away﴾: ﴿مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl). It was also said that it means: they became ones who turn away.

﴿As if they were donkeys﴾: ﴿حُمُرٌ﴾ is the plural of ḥimār (donkey). ﴿Startled﴾: the readers of Medina and Syria read ﴿مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ﴾ with a fatḥah on the fā', while the rest read it with a kasrah. Whoever reads it with a fatḥah, its meaning is "scattered and terrified" (munaffarah maz'ūrah). Whoever reads it with a kasrah, its meaning is "fleeing" (nāfirah). It is said that nafara and istanfara have one meaning, just as 'ajiba and ista'jaba have one meaning.

﴿Fleeing from a lion﴾: Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: "al-qaswarah" means archers, having no singular from its own root. This is also the report of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they are hunters. This is also the report of 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: [they are] [[In "B": min.]] strong men, and every large, powerful thing is called qaswar and qaswarah among the Arabs. From Abu al-Mutawakkil, he said: it is the noise and voices of the people. 'Ikrimah related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: it is the nets of the hunters.

Abu Hurayrah said: it is the lion, and this is the view of 'Ata' and al-Kalbi. That is because wild donkeys, when they see a lion, flee; likewise these polytheists, when they hear the Prophet (ﷺ) reciting the Qur'an, flee from him.

'Ikrimah said: it is the darkness of the night, and the darkness at the beginning of the night is called qaswarah.

﴿Rather, each one of them wants to be given scrolls spread out﴾: the commentators (mufassirun, exegetes) said: the disbelievers of Quraysh said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Let there be at the head of each one of us an open book from Allah stating that you are His messenger, in which we are commanded to follow you."

Al-Kalbi said: the polytheists said: "O Muhammad, it has reached us that a man among the Children of Israel would wake up to find written at his head his sin and its expiation, so bring us the like of that." "Ṣuḥuf" means books, and it is the plural of ṣaḥīfah, and "munashsharah" means spread out (manshūrah).

Al-Kalbi said: the polytheists said: "O Muhammad, it has reached us that a man among the Children of Israel would wake up to find written at his head his sin and its expiation, so bring us the like of that." "Ṣuḥuf" means books, and it is the plural of ṣaḥīfah, and "munashsharah" means spread out (manshūrah).

[Footnote: Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 8/340 as narrated by 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir; see also al-Tabari 29/171.]

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Nay﴾ (they will not be given the scrolls). It was also said: "Truly" — and whatever comes to you of this word, this is its meaning. ﴿Nay, they do not fear the Hereafter﴾, that is, they do not fear the punishment of the Hereafter. The meaning is that if they had feared the Fire, they would not have demanded these signs after the proofs had been established.

﴿Nay﴾, truly. ﴿Indeed it﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿is a reminder﴾, an admonition.

﴿So whoever wills, let him remember it﴾, that is, let him take heed from it.

﴿And they will not remember﴾ — Nafi' and Ya'qub read [tadhkurun] (with the ta') [[addition from "b".]], while the others read it with the ya' — ﴿unless Allah wills﴾. Muqatil said: unless Allah wills guidance for them.

﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, that is, He is worthy that His prohibitions be feared, and worthy to forgive those who fear Him.

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us: Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Umar ibn al-Khattab related to us: Abdullah ibn al-Fadl related to us: Hudbah ibn Khalid related to us: Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning this verse: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, he said: "Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am worthy that I be feared, and that none associate anything with Me; and I am worthy, for whoever fears Me and does not associate anything with Me, that I forgive him.'"
